title: An idle CC session is told it has mail
intention: When mail lands in CC's mailbox while CC's session is idle, the cc shim gets CC's attention by telling it, and only telling it, that it has mail.
why: Lived symptom: the Pi's outage alert, or any bus mail to cc, lands in ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail and sits there while CC is idle, because the only announcer (the PreToolUse `cairn mailcheck` hook) fires only inside an active turn. Akien 2026-10-14: 'then your shim gets the alert and gets your attention ... we only use it (if we can) to tell you that you've got mail.' Measured 2026-10-17: the 'if we can' is yes.
traces_to: Telos 1 (inference compilation): the cc charter's own trace, 'the shim driving CC on idle is the system doing its own work'. It is the CC's-shim rung of the ruled ladder (ground loop → rack → CC's shim → …). Law 7: an outage the Pi raises must reach a mind, not sit unread in a mailbox while CC is idle.
how: After CCShim.deliver() persists an envelope, the shim reads ~/.claude/sessions/*.json for the session named <hostname>_cc_<instance> (the name superclaude gives it). If that session's status is idle, the shim launches one headless `claude -p --model haiku --permission-mode bypassPermissions` whose only act is SendMessage to that name with the text "you've got mail". The content never rides the poke; CC wakes and reads it through the existing `cairn mailcheck` / consume_mail door. A busy session needs no poke (the PreToolUse mailcheck hook already announces mail between tool calls), and pokes coalesce: one per idle stretch, not one per envelope. Every poke is written to the mail ledger beside delivered/consumed, so delivered→poked→consumed can be counted. Measured 2026-10-17 (n=1): this route woke an idle CC session about 10 s after launch, from a systemd user timer. BUILD DETAIL: A Haiku builder needs, and the ticket carries: (a) the place: cairn/devices/cc/shim.py, CCShim.deliver(), immediately after _ledger(delivered); add a method CCShim.poke_if_idle(sessions_dir=None, claude_cmd=None, ledger=None) that deliver() calls; the defaults are Path.home()/'.claude'/'sessions' and ['claude']. (b) The target name is f"{socket.gethostname()}_cc_0" (instance 0, matching _INSTANCE_ROOT). (c) Session lookup: glob <sessions_dir>/*.json, json.loads each, skipping any that fail; the match is data['name'] == target; idle is data['status'] == 'idle'. (d) Coalescing: read the ledger (same file as _ledger); if the last 'poked' line is later in the file than the last 'consumed' line, skip. (e) Launch: subprocess.Popen(claude_cmd + ['-p', '--model', 'haiku', '--permission-mode', 'bypassPermissions', PROMPT], cwd=Path.home()/'dev'/'src'/'cairn', stdin/stdout/stderr=DEVNULL, start_new_session=True), without waiting. PROMPT = 'Call SendMessage exactly once with to="<target>" and message="you\'ve got mail — <mail dir>". Do nothing else.' (f) Ledger lines: {'event':'poked','target':..,'at':..} or {'event':'not-poked','reason':'busy'|'already poked'|'no session named <target>'|'sessions dir unreadable','at':..}. (g) A failure inside poke_if_idle must never stop deliver() returning {'persisted': True}: catch OSError around Popen and ledger 'not-poked' with the error. (h) Proof at cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_an_idle_cc_session_is_told_it_has_mail.py: tooth 1 idle → one launch (stand-in claude_cmd = a tiny script in tmp that appends its argv to a file) and a 'poked' line; tooth 2 busy → no launch; tooth 3 second delivery before consumed → no launch; tooth 4 after a 'consumed' line a new idle delivery pokes again; tooth 5 no matching session / garbage json → no launch, deliver still persists. Use tmp dirs for mail, ledger and sessions; never touch ~/.claude. The existing proofs in cairn/devices/cc/proofs/ must stay green; test_the_shim_delivers_mail.py calls deliver(), so deliver() must accept being run where no sessions dir exists (that's tooth 5's case).
falsifier: Falsifier, from the intent berth and refined. DONE when (1) a deliver() while the named session's record says idle writes a 'poked' ledger line and launches exactly one headless SendMessage to that name; (2) a deliver() while it says busy writes a 'not-poked: busy' line and launches nothing; (3) a second deliver() before any 'consumed' line launches nothing ('not-poked: already poked'); (4) live: a bus message to device 'cc' while CC is idle is followed within 60 s by a 'consumed' ledger line carrying the CC session id. (1)-(3) are a tester proof with a fixture sessions dir and a stand-in claude command; (4) is a measurement recorded at PROVEME. WRONG INTENT if (4) fails twice with the record showing idle (the wake was luck), or a poke is held for approval.

decisions.text: poke_if_idle() takes no arguments: it reads module constants shim._SESSIONS_DIR (~/.claude/sessions), shim._CLAUDE_CMD (['claude']), shim._LEDGER and shim._MAIL_DIR, which proofs reassign; <mail dir> in the PROMPT is str(shim._MAIL_DIR), a path only, never content; an OSError from Popen ledgers not-poked with reason f'launch failed: {exc}'; deliver() calls it only when _MAIL_DIR is still the instance's own mailbox (_INSTANCE_ROOT/'mail'), so a proof that moves only _MAIL_DIR pokes nobody

the existing shim.py constants stand unchanged: _INSTANCE_ROOT = address.instance_path('cc', 0) (~/.cairn/devices/cc/0), _MAIL_DIR = _INSTANCE_ROOT / 'mail', _LEDGER = _INSTANCE_ROOT / 'mail_ledger.jsonl' (the file _ledger() already appends to); the build adds only _SESSIONS_DIR = Path.home()/'.claude'/'sessions' and _CLAUDE_CMD = ['claude'] beside them

two or more session records named the target is its own case: no launch, ledger not-poked with reason f'two sessions are named {target}' (builder can share the name before its rename; never pick one); a torn or non-dict record is skipped, and no match at all or an unreadable dir is reason f'no session named {target}'

every poked / not-poked line carries at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), the same format deliver() and consume_mail() already write, so the live tooth can subtract delivered.at from consumed.at

the new proof's sandbox reassigns shim._INSTANCE_ROOT, _MAIL_DIR (= _INSTANCE_ROOT/'mail'), _LEDGER, _SESSIONS_DIR and _CLAUDE_CMD together, so the guard passes in every sandboxed tooth; one extra tooth (test_mail_outside_the_instance_pokes_nobody) then moves only _MAIL_DIR and asserts no launch, which is the case the older cc proofs are in
